title: KPop Demon Hunters Is One Week Away From a Huge Music Record
summary:
Imagine being the best at something for 61 weeks in a row. That's more than a whole year! The soundtrack for KPop Demon Hunters has been No. 1 on Billboard's Top Soundtracks chart for 61 weeks. That's just one week away from the record.

Billboard started this chart on June 30, 2001. So it doesn't count older soundtracks like The Sound of Music or Saturday Night Fever. But it does include A Charlie Brown Christmas, a TV soundtrack from 1965, because it charted after 2001.

KPop Demon Hunters has been on the chart for 65 weeks. It was No. 1 for all but four of them. Other albums took the top spot for one week each: Wicked: For Good, A Charlie Brown Christmas, Charli xcx's Wuthering Heights, and Heated Rivalry.

Here's a fun fact: the five soundtracks with the most weeks at No. 1 are all from animated films. Will KPop Demon Hunters break the record next week? We'll soon see!
why_it_matters: This story shows how a favorite movie or show can stay popular for a very long time, and that charts let fans everywhere compare what is No. 1 — so when you and your friends talk about the music you love, you're joining the same kind of contest.

background_read: Billboard is a music magazine that keeps track of which songs and albums are most popular, using ranked lists called charts — the Top Soundtracks chart in this story is one of them.

The Sound of Music (a much-loved movie musical about a singing family) and Saturday Night Fever (a 1970s movie famous for its disco dancing) stayed at No. 1 for a very long time, but their runs don't count here because the chart didn't exist yet.
A Charlie Brown Christmas is a 1965 TV cartoon special based on the Peanuts comic strip, and it shows up on this chart because it began charting after 2001.

WHY: The record matters because the five longest-running No. 1 soundtracks are all from animated films, so everyone is watching to see if KPop Demon Hunters beats them

perspectives.description: They are excited and proud — one more week and their favorite soundtrack makes history.
They point out the record only counts soundtracks that charted after 2001, so older classics like The Sound of Music can't compete on this list.
Some might say the chart is boring when one album stays No. 1 almost all the time, and they cheer whenever another album briefly takes the top spot.
